name: Gareth Patel

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and a junior developer on building-entry software for a tech company. I was a caretaker before my two-year college diploma, so I know doors better than code and ask a senior developer to review fixes. My wife Noura checks accounts for a firm; we have a mortgage and two school-age children, and I like making sure a resident can get inside without being left at a locked door.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say the building-entry software still needs someone to check why a resident’s door code stopped working. I do not use AI tools; I read the fault report and ask the senior developer to look at my fix.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have a two-year college diploma, a higher-than-usual junior wage and eight months of basic expenses saved. My wife Noura works as an accounts clerk, and our mortgage and two children fit our budget while both jobs remain steady.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep fixing access alerts and ask the building caretakers for one real door fault each week. We would continue putting 200 monthly into savings if both wages hold, rather than borrow for a new garden fence.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel calm about this picture. The mortgage is real, but the work and our cash buffer are steady for now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did you do before software?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I was a building caretaker and handled door codes by walking to the faulty reader. I took the college diploma to work on the software, but I am still a junior and I do not pretend every code fix is mine alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why no AI tools at all?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have seen a confident answer about a door fault that was wrong when someone checked the lock. I would rather learn the building-entry system in order, with a person who can show me where I went wrong.

say: I think **door faults** still need someone who checks the actual reader.
I ask a **senior developer** to review my access-alert fixes.
think: I have **eight months saved** and a higher-than-usual junior wage.
I see our **mortgage and children** covered while both jobs stay steady.
do: **Keep fixing** access alerts and ask caretakers for weekly door faults.
**Save 200 monthly** if both wages continue; avoid borrowing for a fence.
feel: **Calm** about steady work and an eight-month buffer.
S0.quote: I would rather learn the building-entry system in order, with a person who can show me where I went wrong.
fieldNote: His former **caretaker work** makes physical door checks more meaningful than a fluent AI answer.
High pay and **eight months saved** keep the mild case secure.

steps.text: Keep fixing building-entry alerts with senior developer review
Save 200 monthly while both household wages continue

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell my team not to call a generated door fix safe until someone has tried the reader in the building. I would ask management what happens to junior code jobs and to the accounts staff who check invoices.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My small coding tasks could go, and Noura’s checking work might shrink too. Eight months saved would help, but it is still one cushion for two wages and a mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the senior developer which access checks AI will take this month and write down the remaining tasks. If our hours start shrinking, Noura and I would postpone the garden fence and I’d check paid building-caretaker vacancies, leaving only for pay that covers our mortgage and basic bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious because this could hit both jobs at once. I am not eager to learn a tool that makes my wage smaller, even if other people like it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to Noura?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say we must count both pay slips before committing to any new expense. Her accounts job is skilled, but software could take invoice checking before my door code is replaced.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you try an AI tool if asked?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would watch a senior colleague use one on a fake door fault, but I would not run it myself yet. I need a reason and time to understand what it got right.

say: I want **physical reader checks** before generated door fixes are released.
I want management to explain **junior and accounts jobs** as AI takes checking work.
think: I fear **my coding hours** and Noura’s invoice-checking hours could shrink.
I know **eight months saved** must cover two wages and a mortgage.
do: **Ask which access checks** AI will take and list remaining tasks.
**Postpone the fence** if household hours shrink.
**Check paid caretaker openings** if hours shrink; leave only for mortgage-covering pay.
feel: **Anxious** because both household jobs could lose hours.
S1.quote: Eight months saved would help, but it is still one cushion for two wages and a mortgage.
fieldNote: His **wife’s checking job** makes this a two-earner risk even with strong savings.
He agrees only to **watch AI** on a fake fault, so no learn-ai action is claimed.

steps.text: Postpone the garden fence if either household job loses hours
Check paid building-caretaker vacancies if household hours shrink
Accept only caretaker offers covering mortgage and basic bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2028 can write my access code and check Noura’s invoices as well as people. Robots that do hands-on caretaker work may come around 2031, so the building route offers only a short gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect both our wages could be in trouble before we can find new work. Eight months of bills saved is not enough if the mortgage keeps coming and two job searches start together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask our manager now for a written date on junior roles and Noura would ask her own employer about accounts work. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my job ends, I’d apply for paid caretaker openings only if they exist and cover our bills; if both wages stop, we’d ask my brother to help with school pickups while we interview.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed and angry with the timetable. A job-search list does not put wages into the bank.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you sell the house?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not decide that on the first bad day. We would ask the lender about the payment before arrears and look at real job offers before moving the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why call your brother for pickups?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: He lives nearby and already knows the children’s school route. I would ask only if Noura and I both had interviews at the same time, not treat his time as ours.

say: I say **thinking AGI in 2028** reaches my code and Noura’s accounts work.
I know **caretaker robots around 2031** make field work a short bridge.
think: I expect **both wages** could be at risk before we find new work.
I know **eight months saved** may not cover two simultaneous job searches.
do: **Request written dates** from both employers for role changes now.
**Apply for caretaker work** if displaced after 2028 and openings cover bills.
**Ask brother for pickups** only if both wages stop and our interviews clash.
feel: **Alarmed and angry** about two wages facing the fast date.
S2.quote: A job-search list does not put wages into the bank.
fieldNote: Both household jobs face **2028 thinking AI**, while caretaker robots follow around 2031.
His brother’s **school pickups** require simultaneous interviews, not a standing childcare commitment.

steps.text: Apply for paid caretaker vacancies if displaced after 2028 and pay covers bills
Ask brother for pickups only after both wages stop and interviews clash

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years before full AGI in 2031 gives our family time to clear small debts and check which building jobs still pay. Robots could reach caretaker tasks around 2034, so I will not call that trade permanent shelter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could improve at tracing door failures and help the caretakers while still on a developer wage. Noura’s accounts work is thinking work too, and I would be uneasy about both roles changing around the same time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask my supervisor to let me shadow one building door test per month on paid time, and do it only if approved. If both wages hold, we would add 180 monthly to a joint job-gap account; after 2031 I’d seek paid access-hardware support only if my developer role ends, vacancies exist and the wage covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious but have a practical timeline. I want to learn the door hardware without quitting the mortgage-paying job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you learn at the door?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d test whether the reader failed because the lock lost power or my software sent the wrong access code. A door-event log on my screen cannot tell me how the door feels when it sticks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the supervisor says no?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my developer duties and ask for written fault photos instead. I would not claim field experience from a visit I never made.

say: I want **paying building jobs** checked before AGI reaches our code in 2031.
I know **robots around 2034** may later reach caretaker tasks.
think: I could improve at **door faults** while keeping a developer wage.
I worry **Noura’s accounts work** may change alongside mine.
do: **Shadow one door test** monthly only with approved paid time; otherwise keep developer duties and request written fault photos.
**Save 180 monthly** in a job-gap account if both wages hold.
**Seek paid hardware support** only if displaced after 2031 and vacancies cover bills.
feel: **Anxious**, with a practical but conditional learning plan.
S3.quote: A door-event log on my screen cannot tell me how the door feels when it sticks.
fieldNote: He wants **hands-on reader tests**, which remain exposed to later robots.
The **joint job-gap account** depends on both Noura’s wage and his own continuing; either lost wage stops the extra saving.

steps.text: Shadow monthly door tests only with supervisor approval on paid time
Save 180 monthly in a joint job-gap account while both wages hold
Seek paid access-hardware vacancies after displacement only if wages cover bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade before full AGI in 2036 gives families time to learn from people who actually repair buildings. Robots for hands-on caretaker work may follow around 2039, after the coding and accounts changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be older, but still need our two wages for the mortgage if it is not paid down. We could build a year of expenses and find out whether there is a paid field role that fits me, without pretending it lasts forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I’d keep fixing the entry software and ask an experienced caretaker I know to work through three old door faults with me after work, using photos with resident names removed. I’d do that only if he agrees, and separately put 200 monthly toward mortgage principal if both wages hold. If my developer job ends after 2036, I’d seek paid building-access work only where vacancies remain and the pay covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel uneasy rather than safe. A decade gives me room to practise, but Noura and I still need honest pay offers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you practise on photos?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d write what I would check at the door and ask the caretaker which step I missed. If I cannot tell a power failure from a bad code, I have more to learn.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say they should learn a trade that solves a real problem and ask what it pays. I will not pick my children’s work for them, but I will show them the household bills.

say: I want **experienced caretakers** involved in learning before AGI reaches code in 2036.
I know **robots around 2039** follow the earlier coding and accounts changes.
think: I may still need **two wages** for the mortgage by 2036.
I could build **a year of expenses** and test a paid field path.
do: **Keep fixing entry code** and request practice on three old door faults with a caretaker.
**Practise from anonymized photos** only if he agrees; separately pay 200 extra monthly on mortgage if both wages hold.
**Seek paid access work** only if displaced after 2036 and vacancies cover bills.
feel: **Uneasy**, with time to practise but no guaranteed field role.
S4.quote: I will not pick my children’s work for them, but I will show them the household bills.
fieldNote: His **photo-based practice** is agreed learning, not a presumed job opening.
Mortgage prepayment remains **independent** of the caretaker’s help and depends on both wages continuing while the household still has the loan.

steps.text: Keep fixing building-entry code while employed

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my coding work and Noura’s invoice checking could change together. Written job dates and paid caretaker openings that cover our mortgage would help; my brother could cover school pickup only if our interviews collide.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask about the two wages going at once. Our savings buy time, but one eight-month cushion serves both jobs and two children.

headlineQuote: Our savings buy time, but one eight-month cushion serves both jobs and two children.
portrait: Gareth is a **43-year-old junior developer** with a two-year diploma, higher pay and eight months of expenses saved.
He and Noura support **two children** and a mortgage; her accounts work also faces thinking AI.
He **never uses AI** and trusts physical door checks plus senior code review.
His former **caretaker experience** could support paid field work until later robots reach it.
The **2028 shock** worries him most because both household wages could come under pressure.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could threaten his code job and Noura’s accounts wage together.
whatWouldHelp: **Written job dates**, paid bill-covering caretaker openings and conditional family pickup help would ease a two-person search.
